Subject: Site-wide latency spike + 5xx increase (US-WEST)

Jordan —

We started seeing a sharp increase in end-user latency and an elevated 500/502 rate across our checkout flows hitting US-WEST starting ~08:45 PT. The service graph shows token latencies spiking from ~80ms to 1.2s for a subset of requests; errors are concentrated on region us-west-2 gateway (we've attached sampled traces and the metrics extract). This is impacting two of our largest merchants (Merchant IDs: M-410, M-612).

Our SREs are asking whether you have a cross-region plan ready — we need an ETA on mitigation and whether Redwood can fail traffic to a healthy region while preserving session affinity. We flagged this as P1 internally.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Site-wide latency spike + 5xx increase (US-WEST) — proposed cutover plan

Thanks — I dug into the telemetry and logs. Quick summary:
- Root cause likely overloaded inference pool in us-west-2 for the large merchant shard; KV cache pressure + long-tail context sequences amplified latency.
- us-east-1 nodes show healthy p99s ~120ms and spare capacity.

Proposed plan (can execute in ~20–30 minutes):
1) Validate model variants/quantization parity for Atlas traffic (2 minutes) — confirmed compatible.
2) Canary 10% traffic to us-east-1 for 5 minutes; monitor p95/p99 and 5xx rates.
3) If canary stable, ramp to 50% over next 10 minutes, then 100% if no regressions.
4) Maintain prefix KV cache warmup by routing recent-session tokens to both regions for 30 minutes to reduce cold starts.
5) If any customer-visible errors increase, automatic fallback to us-west-2 for affected affinity keys.

Operational notes:
- We need a short maintenance window ticket and a Drip policy change to allow traffic steering by region (I can push the policy with a rollback flag).
- I'll request a temporary increase in us-east-1 pool to reduce queuing during ramp (estimated +2 GPUs).

I'll own the cutover and monitor metrics (SERV-9201). Marissa/Laura — please prepare exec note and customer comms. Jordan — coordinate timing with Atlas.

Attachments: [cutover-checklist-v1.pdf (pdf, 14KB)]

--
Rishi Malhotra
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clark <emma@atlasretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Atlas cutover complete — preliminary metrics and next steps

Update — cutover executed at 16:10 PT per Rishi's plan. Quick summary of observable impact:
- Traffic split: canary 10% (16:10–16:15) → 50% (16:25) → 100% (16:40).
- p95: reduced from ~780ms pre-cut to ~170ms post-cut; p99 now ~320ms (customer-facing dashboards).
- 5xx rates dropped from 1.8% to 0.12% in us-east-1.
- Minor session-affinity misses observed for ~0.6% of requests during the ramp; automated fallback triggered for affected affinity keys and recovered within ~90s.

Next steps:
- Rishi to run a targeted KV cache warmup job for the two large merchants overnight.
- Marissa to send customer-facing incident summary with timeline and credits proposal (cc execs).
- Jordan to schedule a 30-minute postmortem with Atlas for tomorrow 10:00 PT.

Attachments: [atlas-metrics-09-18.csv (updated), cutover-checklist-v1.pdf]

Thanks team — closing loop with Atlas now.
